bib.title: PivotRL: High Accuracy Agentic Post-Training at Low Compute Cost

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "PivotRL: High Accuracy Agentic Post-Training at Low Compute Cost", Junkeun Yi*, Damon Mosk-Aoyama*, Baihe Huang* (equal contribution), + Gala, Wang, Devare, Bhardwaj, Gupta, Kuchaiev, Jiao, Zhang, Srinivasan (corresponding). NVIDIA / UC Berkeley. First author: Junkeun Yi. Preprint, arXiv:2603.21383v1 [cs.AI], 22 Mar 2026 (page 1 header dated 2026-3-24). No venue.
COVERAGE: 22 of 22 pages read, 59,690 chars, all of it including appendices A and B (proofs) and the reference list (skimmed). Extraction was clean. Figures not rendered; I read only their text captions/axes.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Same-data SFT vs PivotRL, in-domain: PivotRL avg gain over base +14.11 vs +9.94 for SFT (abstract: +4.17 over SFT). Wins on 3 of 4 benchmarks and LOSES on SWE-Bench Verified (SFT 37.40 vs PivotRL 32.67, -4.73).
  number: tau2 44.35 base / 58.44 SFT / 63.81 PivotRL; SWE-V 19.07/37.40/32.67; Terminal-Bench 5.42/13.75/20.00; BrowseComp 2.50/1.50/11.30
  setup: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507, four single-domain training runs, identical prompts and expert trajectories, NeMo-RL and NeMo-Gym. SWE is mean@3 on OpenHands harness. Seed count not reported.
  quote: "PivotRL outperforms SFT on three of four benchmarks, with an average gain of+14.11over Base versus+9.94for SFT." 
  where: Table 1, p.7
- OOD retention: SFT degrades 8 non-agentic benchmarks by -9.83 on average; PivotRL +0.21, with no benchmark worse than -3.12. Worst case is SFT after terminal training: AIME25 86.04 to 21.56, MATH500 -34.50.
  number: -9.83 vs +0.21 (abstract says +10.04 advantage)
  setup: averaged across the four training runs; OOD benchmarks IFBench, AIME25, MATH500, LiveCodeBench, Scicode, MMLU-Pro, MMLU-ProX, WMT24++. Per-domain table 3 p.9.
  quote: "SFT produces an average OOD change of−9.83, with the worst case after terminal-domain training (AIME25 drops by−64.48, MATH500 by−34.50). PivotRL stays near Base across all benchmarks, with an average change of+0.21and no single benchmark dropping more than−3.12."
  where: p.7
- Compute vs E2E RL on SWE-Bench: same accuracy (32.67%) with ~4x fewer rollout turns and ~5.5x less wall-clock, same number of nodes.
  number: ~133K turns (PivotRL, step 130) vs ~542K turns (E2E RL, step ~72)
  setup: SWE-Bench Verified, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507; PivotRL batch 1024 (64 prompts x 16 gens), 1 turn/sample; E2E RL batch 512 (16 x 32), 12-25 turns/trajectory. Single curve (Figure 1), no seeds stated. Only matched at PivotRL's 32.67 level; the paper never reports E2E RL's final/peak accuracy or E2E RL OOD numbers.
  quote: "PivotRL reaches comparable accuracy to E2E RL with∼4×fewer rollout turns and∼5.5×less wall-clock time."
  where: Fig. 1 p.8, Appendix A.2 p.18
- Ablation (tau2-Bench only): removing pivot filtering drops 63.81 to 59.68; removing functional reward (strict exact-match) drops to 57.34, below same-data SFT 58.44. Naive strict local RL "57.34 vs 58.44 SFT" is the motivating baseline.
  number: 63.81 / 59.68 / 57.34 / SFT 58.44 / base 44.35
  quote: "Removing filtering reduces accuracy from63.81to59 .68; removing functional reward yields57.34."
  where: Table 4 p.10, Sec 4.3 p.8; Table 6 p.18 has per-subdomain (Airline/Retail/Telecom)
- Motivating stat: 71% of randomly sampled turns on tau2-bench and SWE-Bench give zero GRPO signal (all-pass or all-fail group).
  quote: "Empirically on 𝜏 2-bench and SWE-Bench,71%of randomly sampled turns yield a0learning signal"
  where: p.3
- Method: offline-profile K rollouts per turn under frozen reference policy; keep turns with variance >0 and mean < lambda_diff ("pivots"); then GRPO on short local rollouts with verifier reward r_func=1[a in M(s)] instead of exact string match. Verifier varies: SWE matches tool-call name only; Terminal uses schema check + string similarity + LLM judge; tau2/BrowseComp details thin.
  where: Sec 3.1 pp.4-5, App A.2 pp.17-18
- Theory (idealised, finite action space): Thm 3.2: natural-gradient norm along the KL path equals sqrt(Var(r))/beta^2, justifying variance filtering. Thm 3.3: functional reward moves mass to acceptable set while preserving ratios within the acceptable set and within its complement, the paper's explanation of OOD retention. Relies on assumption that task-unrelated actions fall in the complement.
  where: pp.5-7, proofs pp.19-22
- Production: used in Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B. Before to after RL stage (which also included other RL envs, so not isolated to PivotRL): tau2 48.00 to 64.00; SWE-V 12.87 to 61.33; Terminal-Bench 1.1 Core 23.33 to 34.17; BrowseComp 13.03 to 25.04.
  where: Table 5 p.12 (stated p.9)
- Data scale: tau2 SFT set 281,774 trajectories over 838 domains; SWE filtered pivots 87,718 samples; BrowseComp 13,215; Terminal ~20,000 (deduplicated). SWE data from MiniMax-M2.5 trajectories (internal). p.17-18

LIMITS
- Authors concede only future work: non-programmatic verifiers (LLM judge, PRMs), dynamic sampling. No limitations section.
- Not shown: seeds/variance/confidence intervals (none reported); E2E RL comparison only on SWE-Bench, one model (30B MoE) and matched at a single accuracy point; no E2E RL OOD results; no SFT compute cost numbers (SFT is assumed cheap); ablation only on tau2-Bench; Table 5 mixes PivotRL with other RL environments and gives no counterfactual; the theory is idealised and the OOD argument is an assumption; PivotRL needs a domain verifier (SWE verifier is deliberately coarse, tool-name only); needs SFT trajectories plus pre-profiling rollouts (cost of offline profiling not counted in the 4x). SFT beats PivotRL on SWE-V in the same-data comparison. Authors are NVIDIA and the data/trajectories are partly internal. Abstract's "+4.17" and "+10.04" (conclusion) do not match the body's 14.11-9.94=4.17 (ok) and 0.21-(-9.83)=10.04 (ok) but the intro text says OOD SFT "-9.48" while Table 2 says -9.83 (internal inconsistency).
- SFT here is single-domain full training on the same data; no mixed-data or replay-regularised SFT baseline to test whether the OOD loss is avoidable by cheaper means.

BUILDS ON: GRPO (Shao et al., 2024); "SFT memorizes, RL generalizes" (Chu et al., 2025); "Retaining by doing" (Chen et al., 2025); RL's Razor (Shenfeld et al., 2025); catastrophic forgetting (Luo et al., 2025b); DAgger (Ross et al., 2011); imitation horizon bound (Rajaraman et al., 2020); "Reuse your flops" prefix conditioning (Setlur et al., 2026); One-token rollout (Ming et al., 2026); verifier idea (Rohatgi et al., 2025); DAPO dynamic sampling (Yu et al., 2025) as future work; ToolACE (Liu et al., 2025b) for data pipeline.

CODE: Algorithm 1 pseudo-code p.5 only (no snippets). Key equations: pivot filter D_adv = {(s,a*): sigma2(s)>0, mu(s)<lambda_diff} (Eq. 5, p.4); r_func(s,a)=1[a in M(s)] (Eq. 6, p.4).

FIGURES: Fig 1 p.8: SWE-Bench accuracy vs cumulative rollout turns and wall-clock time, PivotRL vs E2E RL (the 4x / 5.5x claim). Fig 2 p.10: tau2 accuracy over training for D_adv vs random vs SFT. Fig 3 p.10: per-batch reward std collapses faster under random pivots. All explain the claims faster than prose; figures were not rendered by me.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Math symbols garbled in extraction but readable. Intro cites SFT OOD as -9.48 (p.2) vs -9.83 in Table 2 and p.7; intro also says "+14.111" (footnote marker artifact, i.e. +14.11).

Short verbatim quotes with pages:
1. p.1 abstract: "PivotRL achieves competitive accuracy with E2E RL with4× fewer rollout turns."
2. p.2: "randomly selected intermediate turns frequently provide negligible learning signals; under Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)... sampled actions at such turns often uniformly succeed or fail, yielding a normalized advantage close to zero"
3. p.7: "In every training domain, PivotRL (rl) preserves OOD performance while SFT (sft) causes broad regression—most dramatically after terminal-domain training, where SFT drops AIME25 from86.04to21.56."

Target-note fit hint (for the caller, not a judgement): it directly addresses "SFT vs RL" and "reward design" (functional vs exact-match reward) claims; it is an NVIDIA preprint with single-run numbers, so cite with that setup.
